However, the order could not be issued prior to one Member of the Commission, who formed part of the Coram, demitting office. Therefore, the matter was relisted for hearing. Thereafter, the parties were heard at length, and an order was reserved in the matter on 8.7.2025, and the parties were permitted to file the written notes of arguments within two weeks. A separate order will be issued in Petition No.140/MP/2019. (a) The Petitioner had filed a similar Petition before the Commission, being Petition No. 77/MP/2018, and had simultaneously filed a Petition in UPERC, being Petition No. 1341 of 2018. However, the Petitioner sought to raise fresh issues, which PTC did not agree to. The (f) The Petitioner has failed to establish that a _force majeure_ event as set out under the Procurer(s)-PPA has occurred. The Petitioner can be termed as an ‘Affected Party’ only if PGCIL is affected by a _force majeure_ event enumerated under Article 9.3.1 of the Procurer(s) PPA. Further, the occurrence of such a _force majeure_ event should have been beyond the reasonable control, directly or indirectly, of the Petitioner, which could not have been avoided even if the Petitioner had taken reasonable care or complied with Prudent Utility Practices. (b) The allegation of the Petitioner that PTC has delayed the payment is false. PTC has been making payments on time and, in many cases, before the due dates, at the Petitioner's specific request. The rebate has been voluntarily agreed to by the Petitioner, and there has never been any coercion or duress by PTC. It is a well-settled principle that the party alleging duress must prove it. On the basis of the submissions made by the parties, the following issues arise for our consideration: _“20. It is evident from the above that both Procurer-PPA and PTC PPA dated 25.7.2013 are inextricably linked to each other and the rights and obligations‟ arising out of any one PPA are reflected in the other PPA. Further, the LOI issued by UPPCL on 22.5.2013 had recognised the generating station of the Petitioner as the source for supply of power to it through PTC. It is also undisputed that PTC had supplied power to Respondent, UPPCL/UP discoms from the generating station of the Petitioner in terms of the said LOI. Thus, the LOI dated 22.5.2013 read with the provisions of the said PPAs unambiguously establish the nexus between the generating company of the Petitioner and the Respondent discoms, even though power was supplied through PTC, which is an inter-State trading licensee. Hence, the contention of Respondent, UPPCL that it has no privity of contract or arrangement with the Petitioner lacks merit. We, therefore, hold that the present Petition filed by the Petitioner for adjudication of disputes against Respondent, UPPCL/UP discoms is maintainable under Section 79(1)(b) read with Section 79(1)(f) of the 2003 Act.”_ 55. The Commission, after hearing the parties on 17.9.2019, directed the Petitioner and PTC to undertake reconciliation and submit the reconciliation statement. It is observed that the parties have not been able to reconcile their claims. The Petitioner and PTC have filed statements, but those statements are not on the basis of any reconciliation between them, and they are reiterations of their initial claims. 118.
